rule: A landlord must provide reasonable prior notice before entering a rented premises. Entering without notice violates the tenant's right to peaceful enjoyment under Kerala Buildings Lease and Rent Control Act.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act 1965

rule: A minimum of 30 days written notice is required before eviction proceedings under Kerala Rent Control Act. Notice periods below 30 days are not legally enforceable.
source: Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act 1965, Section 11

rule: Security deposit exceeding 3 months rent is considered excessive. Under Model Tenancy Act 2021, deposits above this threshold can be challenged.
A clause allowing one party to unilaterally amend contract terms without the other party's consent is generally unenforceable under Indian Contract Act 1872.
Requiring dispute resolution exclusively in a city inaccessible to the weaker party may be challenged as an unfair contract term under Consumer Protection Act 2019.
An employee cannot waive their right to gratuity by contract. Any clause forfeiting gratuity entitlement is void under Payment of Gratuity Act 1972.
Automatic renewal clauses without adequate prior notice to the other party may be considered unfair. Reasonable notice of at least 30 days before renewal is standard practice.
